extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Maritime Executive; maritime industry professionals and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: A news report about Francesco Schettino's petition for early release (semi-liberty) from a 16-year prison sentence for his role in the Costa Concordia disaster, including legal and public-reaction context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for 'semi-liberty' under Italian law
rubrics_metrics.description: "Under Italian law, Schettino filed for early release into a state of 'semi-liberty' whereby he would be out of prison for the remainder of his sentence. This is available after the prisoner has served at least half their time in jail and has demonstrated good behavior.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key legal eligibility requirements stated on the page: (1) prisoner must have served at least half their sentence, and (2) must have demonstrated good behavior. Practically, a petition is filed and a court hearing is set to decide the request (article notes a hearing on March 4). The page frames 'semi-liberty' as release for the remainder of the sentence contingent on these conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction grounds and resulting sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Schettino was sentenced in February 2015 to 16 years in prison for dereliction of duty, multiple counts of manslaughter, causing a shipwreck, and abandoning his passengers.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific convictions listed are the factual/legal basis for the 16-year sentence; these convictions are the operative background for any release petition and may bear on how a court views eligibility for leniency or semi-liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals/exhaustion of remedies and custody status
rubrics_metrics.description: "His appeals were exhausted in 2017. He was ordered to surrender at a prison in Rome.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page indicates appeals were completed and he is in custody — factual procedural posture relevant to timing and availability of post-conviction remedies such as semi-liberty. While not framed as a legal criterion for semi-liberty, appeals/exhaustion and actual incarceration status are material to the release process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reaction / victim impact as contextual factor
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Italian media reports there are mixed reactions. The protests are expected to grow in advance of a court hearing. In addition to the 32 who died, many people were injured and carry emotional scars from the disaster.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not presented as a formal legal requirement, the article highlights public outrage, protests, and victim harm as salient contextual factors that may influence the public and political environment surrounding a release hearing. Use caution: this is contextual influence rather than a codified legal criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural step: court hearing to decide release
rubrics_metrics.description: "An Italian court has set a hearing for March 4 to decide if Schettino will win his release from prison.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page identifies a concrete procedural milestone — a court hearing date — as the forum where the semi-liberty petition will be adjudicated. This underscores that eligibility triggers a judicial determination rather than automatic administrative relief.
